statements.status_notes: Debian's python3-cryptography 43.0.0-3+deb13u1, the build this image ships, includes the upstream fix for the missing subgroup validation of SECT curve public keys, first released in cryptography 46.0.5. See https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-26007

This OpenSSL flaw in RFC 7250 raw public key handshakes affects OpenSSL 3.2, 3.3 and 3.4 (https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20250211.txt). It is reported against cryptography because the project's PyPI wheels from 42.0.0 to 44.0.0 bundle an affected OpenSSL (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-79v4-65xg-pq4g). This image ships Debian's python3-cryptography 43.0.0-3+deb13u1, which is built from source and links the system OpenSSL 3.5.7, so the bundled copy is not present.

The advisory covers the copy of OpenSSL that the cryptography project statically links into its PyPI wheels before 48.0.1 (OpenSSL advisory https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20260609.txt, fixed in OpenSSL 3.5.7), and states that builds from source are not affected. This image ships cryptography built from source: Debian's python3-cryptography 43.0.0-3+deb13u1 links the system OpenSSL 3.5.7, and the Alpine py3.14-cryptography 47.0.0-r0 package links the system OpenSSL 3.5.9, so the bundled copy is not present. See https://github.com/pyca/cryptography/security/advisories/GHSA-537c-gmf6-5ccf

Improper name constraint validation affecting cryptography 45.0.0 up to but not including 49.0.0, first fixed in 49.0.0. This image keeps cryptography at the version upstream GitLab CNG pins for the matching release tag, so the crypto stack matches the one GitLab validated; taking 49.0.0 would put this image three major versions ahead of CNG. The code is reachable: google-auth imports cryptography to sign service account credentials under gsutil. Resolves when CNG moves to cryptography 49.0.0 or later.

Observable timing discrepancy affecting cryptography 44.0.0 up to but not including 50.0.0, first fixed in 50.0.0. This image keeps cryptography at the version upstream GitLab CNG pins for the matching release tag, so the crypto stack matches the one GitLab validated; taking 50.0.0 would put this image four major versions ahead of CNG. The code is reachable: google-auth imports cryptography to sign service account credentials under gsutil. Resolves when CNG moves to cryptography 50.0.0 or later.

CVE alias of GHSA-537c-gmf6-5ccf, recorded so this document matches whichever identifier a scanner reports. The flaw is an out-of-bounds read in the OpenSSL copy that the cryptography project bundles into its prebuilt manylinux wheels, fixed in the 48.0.1 wheel. The advisory states that source installs are unaffected, because they link the system OpenSSL instead. This image builds cryptography from source, so it links the patched system OpenSSL and the vulnerable bundled copy is not present.
